rubrics.justification: The response explicitly states no image was provided and relies almost entirely on the Gardner score rather than the actual image. It also inaccurately paraphrases TE grade B as 'few cells forming a loose epithelium,' which is closer to a C description than standard B.

It integrates most relevant factors well, including age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, prior live birth, sperm parameters, BMI, and endometrium, and connects them to prognosis, though some interactions are somewhat generalized.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with conclusions generally supported by the presented factors. Minor issues include somewhat optimistic interpretation of embryo quality and probability framing.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice, especially support for single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst. Minor deviations include overstatement of embryo quality and a somewhat casual suggestion of PGT-A in a low-risk 28-year-old.

Provides clear practical recommendations for transfer, luteal support, lifestyle counseling, and future planning. It is useful clinically, though some advice remains generic rather than highly individualized.
